title: Piano lessons that fizzle and a brief stint on trumpet
summary: His father wants him on piano; repeated moves mean new teachers and starting over, then a short try at trumpet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So by the time you were in like junior high school, had you decided on your career path so to speak?

Well we can start a little bit earlier than that. When we moved to Buffalo my father decided I was going to be a piano player. And I took piano lessons. And we lived in downtown Buffalo for a couple of years, and I started learning out of the Thompson method. And then in 1952 we moved to Cheektowaga, New York, which is a suburb of Buffalo, and every time we moved I’d have to change piano teachers, and that piano teacher would start me over with their method. So like I was becoming very disenchanted. You know like okay I got to this point, but no, I want to start you the way I teach so then we’d start over. Then we moved here, to Cortland, in 1953, and I started again on the piano. By this time I was becoming very disenchanted, although I wish I had

stuck with it because it sure was a lot easier to play an acoustic piano than it was to lug that stuff around. So anyway, that thing kind of fizzled out. Then I took up the trumpet. That lasted for a couple of years, right up here at Parker School, a couple of blocks away. And that was okay but that didn’t work out either. And in 1956 Tommy and Jimmy Dorsey, the Dorsey Brothers Orchestra, came to Cortland. You went by it on your way here, it’s a place called Skateland. It was a roller skating rink. Now it’s just a vacant building. It became Grossman’s Lumber and it’s just a building up there. Well we went in that summer, and I still hadn’t focused on — my father just said, “he hasn’t got it, he just doesn’t have it man, you know I mean he’s not going to be a musician.” Because I had dropped two instruments.
But he wanted you to be.
